items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So I heard Joe Williams with Count Basie.

ctx.x: And I don’t know where it came from.

Yeah. There’s a glow. I don’t know where it comes from either but yeah, I sure do recognize it in some people. He was one of the first people that I heard with big bands, because my father played Count Basie. So I heard Joe Williams with Count Basie. And he’s got a very distinctive sound. Maybe I read this somewhere but he was like the first gentleman blues singer. You know, articulate. His notes were right on. He didn’t — I mean I don’t know what Mr. Williams did but he never sounded like he was drunk. A lot of…
Oh yeah. Okay I got one more for you here. This has always mystified me.

items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: So I saw Joe Williams sing a lot of times.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well it’s hard to teach somebody something that you don’t know about. I mean they don’t know about it. They don’t know about maybe getting kicked off the bandstand.

You know? “Nice try baby, come back another time.” So that’ll either make you quit or go home and work on it. Or you know I went to watch before I ever tried to do this, I was a fan. So I saw Joe Williams sing a lot of times. And I wasn’t just listening to him sing, I would watch the way he would get up from the stool. I mean you do something a little different when you’re on stage, because they realized that yeah you’re listening to me but you’re also looking at me. So you have to present yourself in a certain…
